alder-ui v0.5.0

A light-DOM, token-based design system with shadcn/ui's look (new-york-v4, neutral): plain CSS in @layer al, plus small scripts that progressively enhance the interactive elements. This page links the built al.css and al.js and shows every element's demo as it renders. The per-element pages, which also show the no-JavaScript fallbacks, are in demo/. Source and docs: github.com/tapegram/alder-ui.

Colour tokens

shadcn's canonical neutral theme, verbatim oklch values. Re-theme by pasting a shadcn or tweakcn export after al.css.

al-button

One look, three forms. Put a native <button> inside: it works with no JavaScript (Alder renders the button inside for you). An <a> inside makes a link that looks like a button. The element alone is presentational: it looks like a button but is not one until a framework gives it a role, focus and Enter/Space handling.

al-input

The markup Alder renders for <al-input field="title" label="Title" />: a real <label> around the input, then the help text (when given) and the ul.errors list. help is a <small class="help">; invalid colours the border.

                                          al-dialog

                                          A modal dialog around a native <dialog> that you write: Alder's renderer writes it for you (heading, close button and all), other stacks write it by hand, as here. Opened by commandfor / command="show-modal" on a button. The no-JS form comes first.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          A link to the dialog's id shows it (:target); the close link # hides it. No script, no invoker commands.

                                          al-popover

                                          A floating panel anchored to its invoker. placement picks the side, offset the gap, anchor another anchor by id; the browser flips it when there is no room.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          popovertarget and the popover attribute are the platform's: no script runs. (Only the placement needs a browser with CSS anchor positioning.)

                                          Opened by popovertarget. Escape or a click outside closes it.

                                          Placements and offsets

                                          Above, with a medium gap. To the left, with a large gap. To the right. Anchored to the Top button, not its invoker.

                                          Title and description

                                          A heading inside the popover is its title and a paragraph its description.

                                          Dimensions

                                          Set the dimensions for the layer.

                                          al-menu

                                          A popover of links or buttons. The optional script adds menu roles, roving arrow keys and closing on select.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          The menu is a popover of plain links; the platform opens and closes it. No roles or arrow keys (those come from al-menu.js).

                                          Profile Settings

                                          Enhanced

                                          With the script: arrow keys, Home/End, focus on the first item, closes on select. Try it with the keyboard. An <hr> is a separator; data-variant="destructive" tints an item (and its icon) with the destructive colour.

                                          Edit Duplicate

                                          Anchored elsewhere

                                          anchor names another element by id; the menu opens against it, not its invoker (this needs al.js).

                                          Profile Settings

                                          al-tabs

                                          Tabs backed by a radio group: they work with no script; the script builds the ARIA tabs pattern from them: a tablist of button role=tab (aria-selected, aria-controls, a roving tabindex) before the panels, the labels hidden, tabpanel with aria-labelledby. al-tab holds a label with a radio and its al-panel.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          The radio group selects the tab and the arrow keys move between tabs; the server writes checked on the radio it picks.

                                          The overview panel. The details panel.

                                          With variant="line" the checked label is underlined; without the script there is no muted pill (the labels and panels share one flex row).

                                          The overview panel. The details panel.

                                          Enhanced

                                          With the script: the ARIA roles and states, Home and End, selected picks the open tab (here the second), and a name on the tab supplies the radio's group.

                                          Three posts. Twelve comments (selected by the server). Settings live here.

                                          Line

                                          variant="line" drops the muted pill and underlines the active tab.

                                          The overview panel. The details panel.

                                          al-toast

                                          A transient message in a corner region. The script shows the region, sets role="status" and closes the toast after timeout.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          The toast region is a hidden popover until the script shows it, so the server also renders the message in the page as an al-alert:

                                          Post saved.

                                          Enhanced

                                          With the script, each region is shown when its toast connects. On demo/toast.html these are sticky (timeout="0") so you can see all four variants at all four corners; the default timeout is 5000 ms and the toast closes itself. Text or a strong before the first block (div, p, list) is the title and the blocks are the description; a one-line message, even with inline elements, is all title. A toast with no variant has no icon.

                                          Timeout and motion

                                          A toast slides in from its region's edge and, when it closes, slides back out before it is removed (not with reduced motion). This one closes after 3000 ms.

                                          al-tooltip

                                          A text-only hint for the element named by for, shown on hover and focus.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          The tooltip stays hidden; put the same text in a title on the trigger.

                                          Enhanced

                                          Hover or focus the button: the tooltip is anchored to it, and the button gains aria-describedby. Escape hides it.

                                          Saves without publishing

                                          al-devpanel

                                          Alder's developer bar, as a design-system element: a collapsed bar and an expanded tabbed panel, server-rendered, with monospace code.

                                          Without JavaScript

                                          Open, every section shows (no tab switching); collapsed, only the bar. The server picks with open.
